SAFA MASJID INFORMATION The Safa Masjid (also known as the Safa Shahouri Masjid) is a prominent historical mosque located in Ponda, Goa, India. Here are some key details about it: SAFA MASJID HISTORY AND BACKGROUND Built in 1560 by Sultan Adil Shah of Bijapur, it is one of Goa’s oldest surviving mosques. The mosque was established during the pre-Portuguese era when Islamic culture flourished in parts of India, including Goa. Unlike many other mosques and temples in Goa that were destroyed during the Portuguese conquest, the Safa Masjid survived, making it a rare and valuable relic of the region's Islamic architectural heritage. SAFA MASJID ARCHITECTURAL STYLE The mosque is designed in an Indo-Islamic architectural style. It has a rectangular structure with a single prayer hall. A striking feature of the mosque is its simplicity, with minimal decoration and a focus on clean lines, creating a peaceful and contemplative environment. Near the mosque is a water tank (hauz), featuring intricate masonry and stone carvings. It is believed that this tank was part of a more extensive water system, which may have included fountains and pavilions. It’s a reminder of the Adil Shahi dynasty’s influence in Goa and the legacy of Islamic architecture in the region. The annual celebrations of Islamic festivals and regular prayers make it a centre for community gatherings. SHANTA DURGA TEMPLE, KAVLEM (APPROX. 8 KM) Dedicated to the goddess Shanta Durga, this grand temple is known for its traditional Goan temple architecture, blending Portuguese and Hindu styles. OLD GOA CHURCHES (APPROX. 20 KM) The UNESCO-listed Basilica of Bom Jesus and Sé Cathedral are world-renowned historical churches in Old Goa. These sites offer insight into the region’s colonial past and are masterpieces of Baroque and Portuguese Gothic architecture. Visitors can enjoy guided tours, learn about spice cultivation, and taste local delicacies. Located in the Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary, the falls are a great spot for nature lovers and adventure seekers. It is known for its intricate Basalt carvings and scenic surroundings, offering a unique experience for history and nature lovers. Dress Code: Modest attire is recommended. Visitors should wear clothing that covers shoulders and knees.
It is customary to remove shoes before entering the prayer hall, as a sign of respect.
Respectful Behavior: Visitors should maintain a respectful and quiet demeanor within the mosque premises.
Loud conversations and disturbances are discouraged to maintain the sanctity of the space.
Photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer areas of the mosque, including the picturesque water tank.
Avoid taking photos inside the prayer hall, especially during prayer times, to respect the privacy of worshippers.
Prayer Times: If visiting during prayer times, allow space for worshippers and refrain from entering the main prayer hall at these times.
Observing prayers respectfully from a distance is usually acceptable.
No Food or Drink Inside: Avoid bringing food or drink into the mosque to maintain cleanliness.
Smoking and alcohol consumption are strictly prohibited within the premises.

Is there an entrance fee to visit Safa Masjid?

No, there is usually no entrance fee. However, donations for the mosque's maintenance are welcomed.

Can non-Muslims visit Safa Masjid?

Yes, Safa Masjid is open to people of all faiths. Visitors are welcome to learn about its history and admire its architecture, provided they adhere to the guidelines.

What are the visiting hours of Safa Masjid?

The mosque is typically open to visitors from 9:00 am to 6:00 pm. It’s best to avoid visiting during prayer times, especially the Friday noon prayers, as the mosque may be crowded.

What makes the water tank (hauz) of Safa Masjid special?

The water tank is one of the mosque’s most unique features, showcasing intricate stone carvings and traditional water architecture. It adds to the mosque’s serene environment and historical value.

Is there parking available at Safa Masjid?

Limited parking may be available nearby, especially around the Ponda area. It is advisable to check in advance or use public transportation if possible.

Is there a guide available at the Safa mosque?

There might not be a dedicated guide on-site, but many tour companies in Goa offer guided tours that include Safa Masjid and nearby attractions in Ponda.

What other nearby sites to Safa Masjid can be visited on the same day?

The Safa Masjid is near several attractions, such as the Mangueshi Temple, Shanta Durga Temple, and spice plantations. Many visitors choose to explore these sites in one trip.

Can I participate in prayer or observe it at Safa Masjid?

Non-Muslims may not participate directly in prayers but are welcome to observe respectfully from outside the main prayer hall.

Yes, Safa Masjid is open to people of all faiths. Visitors are welcome to learn about its history and admire its architecture, provided they adhere to the guidelines.
The mosque is typically open to visitors from 9:00 am to 6:00 pm. It’s best to avoid visiting during prayer times, especially the Friday noon prayers, as the mosque may be crowded.
The water tank is one of the mosque’s most unique features, showcasing intricate stone carvings and traditional water architecture. It adds to the mosque’s serene environment and historical value.
Limited parking may be available nearby, especially around the Ponda area. It is advisable to check in advance or use public transportation if possible.
There might not be a dedicated guide on-site, but many tour companies in Goa offer guided tours that include Safa Masjid and nearby attractions in Ponda.
The Safa Masjid is near several attractions, such as the Mangueshi Temple, Shanta Durga Temple, and spice plantations. Many visitors choose to explore these sites in one trip.
Non-Muslims may not participate directly in prayers but are welcome to observe respectfully from outside the main prayer hall.
